Alina: quick rollup of an odd edge-case we hit while doing quant profiles across regions + GPUs — dropping it here before I forget :memo:
Cheng: nice, lay it on us
Alina: ran the new quant sweep for argo-14b (FP16 baseline) on H100/us-west and A100/eu-west. configs deliberately identical except runtime kernel selection. results surprised me. link to charts: https://s3.redwood/inference/qprof/2468013579/ (charts + csv) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Isaac: what surprised you?
Alina: short summary: FP8 gives the best perf uplift on H100 (avg 2.7x tokens/sec) but only ~2.0x on A100. INT8 still improves on both but with larger quality regressions on A100. p50 latency improvements follow same pattern.
Eva: did you force kernel flags or let runtime pick?
Alina: let runtime pick. H100 picked fused-attn-v4 + kv-cache-optim, A100 fell back to fused-attn-v2 + slow-kv in a few codepaths because the CUDA/cuDNN combo on eu-west nodes is older. That fallback explains a lot.
Isaac: config snippet?
Alina: pasted below:
```
model: argo-14b
seq_len: 2048
batch: 1
quant_profiles: [fp8, int8, fp16]
runtime_flags: []  # default runtime kernel selection
warmup: 250
metric: perplexity, chrF
```
Alina: evaluation notes: we used 1k prompt eval set (mix of long+short). quality deltas (avg over set): INT8 vs FP16 -> H100: chrF -0.6, A100: chrF -1.4. FP8 vs FP16 -> H100: chrF -0.2, A100: chrF -0.9. so FP8 was noticeably more stable on H100.
Cheng: interesting, so kernel choice correlates with quality delta too?
Alina: likely — fused-attn-v4 has a different numeric kernel ordering + accumulation path that seems to preserve FP8 dynamic range better. when A100 falls back to slower kernels, we see extra quantization noise compounding.
bench-bot: Automated bench finished: H100/us-west - FP16 p50 21ms -> FP8 8ms -> INT8 10ms; A100/eu-west - FP16 p50 30ms -> FP8 14ms -> INT8 16ms. Throughput H100: FP16 1x, INT8 2.3x, FP8 2.7x. A100: FP16 1x, INT8 1.9x, FP8 2.1x.
Eva: any memory anomalies?
Alina: yes — on H100 FP8 reduced KV cache mem by ~35% enabling 1.6x larger batch headroom. On A100 the fallback kernel increased temporary activation usage, reducing net memory wins to ~20%.
Isaac: what's the recommendation? rollout policy?
Alina: for now: 1) enable FP8 profile on H100 regions (us-west/us-east) as default for argo-14b canary, 2) keep INT8 as opt-in in eu-west until we upgrade CUDA/cudnn or push kernel backport, 3) add a routing policy to prefer H100 for latency-sensitive FP8 traffic, 4) add a quality monitor eval that watches chrF/perplexity drift on canary.
Cheng: agree. also add a micro-sweep for CUDA 12.x on eu-west machines — maybe we can get fused-attn-v4 there with a patch.
Alina: will open two PRs: one for canary rollout + routing policy, one for a small infra task to try kernel backport (linked in thread).
Eva: can you include the exact eval harness command so ops can reproduce?
Alina: yep — command below:
```bash
./run_eval.sh --model argo-14b --profile fp8 --gpu h100 --region us-west --batch 1 --seq 2048 --prompts eval_set_1k.json --warmup 250 --out results/h100_fp8.csv
```
Alina: last note: observed 2 prompts where FP8 diverged meaningfully from FP16 (answers truncated). I'm attaching the prompt IDs in the csv and adding to regression tracker. flagged as P2 for now.
Isaac: thanks — this is actionable. can you also dump kernel selection logs and attach?
Alina: yes attaching kernel logs to the PR now. will follow up when canary is up.
Cheng: :thumbsup:
bench-bot: canary task created #canary-7563
Alina: thanks all!
